title: 为什么年纪越大，时间过得越快
title_en: Why Time Seems to Speed Up as We Get Older
summary_zh: 为什么长大后一年好像一眨眼就过去？比起「一年占人生的比例变小」，新鲜经历和记忆更能解释这种感觉。读完你会明白其中的道理，还能学会写一段留有余地的说明文。
body: Almost everyone over thirty has said it at some point: the years seem to pass more quickly than they used to, and a summer that once felt endless now disappears in what feels like a few weeks. The clock, of course, has not changed, so the explanation must lie in how we experience and remember time. One popular idea is proportional: a year is a huge slice of a seven-year-old's life but a thin one of a fifty-year-old's, so it feels smaller as we age. The idea is neat, but on its own it explains rather little, since nobody actually experiences their life as a fraction. A more convincing account focuses on novelty and memory. When we are young, a great deal of what happens is new: the first day at a school, the first trip abroad, the first job. New experiences tend to be stored in rich detail, and when we look back, a period full of such memories seems long. As adult life settles into routines, many weeks resemble one another so closely that they leave few distinct traces behind. Looking back on a year like that, the mind finds little to measure it by, and the year seems to have shrunk. There is an odd twist here, because the same routine weeks can drag while we are living through them and then vanish once they are over. If this account is broadly right, the remedy is not to slow the clock but to give memory more to hold on to. Learning a skill, travelling somewhere unfamiliar or simply changing a daily route can make a stretch of time feel fuller in hindsight. Researchers still debate the details, but the practical lesson is encouraging: we cannot add hours to the day, yet we may be able to make the hours we have feel longer.

questions.prompt: What does the text mainly explain?
options: Why time may feel faster as we age, and what might help
Why children sleep more than adults
Why summers are shorter than they used to be
questions.evidence: the explanation must lie in how we experience and remember time

questions.prompt: Why does the writer say the proportional idea "explains rather little"?
options: The maths behind it is wrong
People do not actually feel their life as a fraction
questions.evidence: nobody actually experiences their life as a fraction

questions.prompt: What does "in hindsight" mean in "feel fuller in hindsight"?
options: when you look back on it later

questions.prompt: According to the text, what can make a stretch of time feel fuller?
options: Learning a skill or travelling somewhere unfamiliar
questions.evidence: Learning a skill, travelling somewhere unfamiliar or simply changing a daily route

vocabulary.example: The price is proportional to the size of the room.
The novelty of the new phone wore off after a week.
I have a distinct memory of my first day at school.
The twins resemble each other closely.
With hindsight, we should have left earlier.

expressions.note: 泛指某个时刻：At some point, everyone feels lost.
常用来说“仅凭这一点还不够”。
settle into a routine / a new job：慢慢习惯下来。
live through 常指经历一段时期，尤其是难熬的时期。
可以是实物，也可以是记忆、希望。
回顾时用：In hindsight, it was a good decision.

knowledge.quote: Looking back on a year like that, the mind finds little to measure it by
knowledge.explanation: 现在分词短语 Looking back… 作状语，逻辑主语和主句主语 the mind 一致，表示“回顾时”。

knowledge.quote: many weeks resemble one another so closely that they leave few distinct traces behind
knowledge.explanation: so + 副词 + that… 表示“如此……以至于”，前面说程度，后面说结果。

knowledge.quote: If this account is broadly right, the remedy is not to slow the clock but to give memory more to hold on to.
knowledge.explanation: 真实条件句：如果这种解释大体对，那么……；主句用 not A but B 对比两种做法。

speaking: 用 1 分钟说说：你觉得哪一年过得特别快、哪一年特别慢？为什么？用上 in hindsight 和 settle into。
writing: 用 200–250 词写一段说明文，解释一个常见的「感觉」（如时间变快、周一特别长）背后可能的原因。说「目前的解释」时要留有余地，至少用一个 so… that… 句子。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 we cannot …, yet we may be able to … 写一句话，给出一个现实的建议。
task.model: we cannot add hours to the day, yet we may be able to make the hours we have feel longer
